subject: Export patterns, sampling criteria, and provenance clarification for admin activity evidence
messages:
From: Compliance Ops <compliance@novamed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Audits R Us <audits@audits-r-us.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: admin activity evidence — format, sample windows, and provenance

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Novamed's audit team is finalizing the SIG/SOC2 evidence checklist and we need clarification on exactly how Redwood can deliver admin activity proof material for the "operator/admin actions" and "privileged access" categories. Specifically:

- Can you confirm the export formats you support (NDJSON/Parquet/CSV), compression options, and whether we can request delta vs full snapshot exports?
- For long-running audits, we sometimes request sampled slices. What's your supported sampling strategy (time-window sampling, event-sampling, or per-tenant percent-based)? Can you attest to reproducible sampling with a seed or manifest?
- Provenance: we need signed manifests (SHA256) and a simple chain-of-custody record (who requested, who pulled, transport method).
- PII redaction: what fields are redacted by default and what can be left unredacted under an approved NDA?

Can you provide a short runbook and an estimate for lead time and any cost implications for on-demand snapshots vs scheduled exports? Audits R Us will be coordinating the evidence intake and we may need the files uploaded to a temporary SFTP endpoint.

Appreciate a succinct bulletized response we can attach to our SIG packet.

Best,
Maya Patel
Compliance Ops, Novamed
compliance@novamed.com

---
Attachment: novamed_evidence_requirements_v2.pdf (pdf, 180KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: admin activity evidence — format, sample windows, and provenance

Maya — thanks for the clear list. Below is a compact runbook and options matrix; please tell us which combination you prefer and we will schedule a dry-run export. Short answers first, then options.

Summary (short):
- Supported export formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), Parquet (columnar), CSV (flat). All can be gzipped. Parquet recommended for large full snapshots, NDJSON for event streaming and small slices.
- Snapshot modes: full snapshot (timeboxed), delta window (per-day deltas), and streaming harvest (Kafka-style delivery to a customer sink).
- Sampling strategies: time-window sampling (explicit start/end UTC), event-sampling (every Nth event with reproducible manifest), and tenant-percent sampling (deterministic hashing by tenant id with seed). We provide a signed manifest describing the sampling seed and checksum.
- Provenance: Signed manifest (SHA256) + HMAC over manifest, export audit record (who requested, who authorized, SFTP/HTTPS endpoint, delivery timestamp).
- PII redaction: default export masks user email and IPs; under NDA we can include email, user_id, and device_id but will redact session tokens and secrets. Redaction policy documented in the attached matrix.

Runbook (what to expect):
1) Confirm scope: categories (operator actions, privilege grants, role changes), timebox (UTC start/end), and format.
2) Choose mode: on-demand full snapshot (typical lead 48–72 business hours for >30M events), delta harvest (24–48 hours), or scheduled daily snapshots (24 hours).
3) Sampling: specify sampling type + parameters (e.g., time-window: 2026-06-01T00:00Z/2026-06-30T23:59Z; event-sample: every 1000th event with seed=7231).
4) Deliverables: files (NDJSON.gz or Parquet.gz), signed manifest (manifest.json.sig), export manifest checksum file (manifest.sha256), and export-audit.csv listing the export operation metadata.
5) Transport: SFTP (preferred for large bundles), pre-signed HTTPS, or direct upload to a customer bucket (AWS/GCP/Azure). We support encrypted transfer (TLS + server-side encryption).

Notes on provenance and attestation:
- Every export is stamped with an immutable export_id and is recorded in our admin evidence ledger. We can produce an attestation statement that includes the export_id, SHA256 checksums, operator ids of who assembled the bundle, and a signed timestamp.
- For sampled exports, we include a reproducibility block in the manifest: sampling method, seed, hash function used, and deterministic sorting key so a third party can confirm the sample was derived from the stated population.

Cost/lead time:
- Small slices (<10M events): usually same-day or 24h with no additional charge.
- Large snapshots (>100M events) or expedited requests: 48–72h and may incur a handling fee (estimate provided after scope confirmation).

Deliverable attachments: we attached a quick matrix (admin_activity_export_matrix.csv) showing fields exported, default redaction, and optional exposures under NDA. Also attached a one-page PDF outlining formats and delivery options.

Next steps:
- Confirm scope (timebox + categories) and preferred format/transport.
- If sampling, confirm sampling parameters and whether you require a dry-run manifest.

Cc'ing Kimberly for PII redaction exceptions and Grace for chain-of-custody & legal hold questions.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: admin activity evidence — format, sample windows, and provenance

Ben / Maya,

One quick addition on redaction & retention:
- Retention/Legal hold: If Novamed needs a legal hold for a specific timeframe, we can preserve export snapshots for up to 2 years in a locked evidence archive (immutable storage). Standard retention is 90 days for operational telemetry.
- PII checklist: Under NDA we can include user email and device identifiers but session tokens, OAuth refresh tokens, and raw passwords are always stripped. We can provide a per-field redaction map keyed to column names in the matrix.
- Access control: any unredacted artifact requires a signed access request (SLA form HS-56324) + proof of authorization (signed PDF).

Ben — can your team add a sample manifest and one reproducible sampling example to the Google Drive folder? I'll sign off on the redaction exceptions once the access control steps are appended.

Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Security | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
